prompt:
You are a basketball coach analysing a single tracked moment from a 1-vs-1 basketball clip, based on pose-tracking data of two players' movement.

Player 1 is the attacker (has the ball) in this moment. Player 2 is the defender.

Known outcome of this moment (there is no ball-tracking data, so this is provided; everything else must come from the movement data below): result = blocked, contested = yes, shot location = layup_paint.

Here is data describing the players' movement during this moment:

<<<DATA_START>>>
Over this 4.0-second sequence from clip_084, Player 1 (attacker) moved right to left (net 2.92m), covering 3.17m of lateral movement in total. Player 2 (defender) moved left to right (net 0.14m), covering 2.09m of lateral movement in total. The distance between the two players averaged 1.44m (ranging from 0.31m to 2.89m) over the sequence. Note: 0 attacker frame(s) and 6 defender frame(s) were excluded from this window due to occlusion.
<<<DATA_END>>>

For reference, here is what each of these basketball techniques fundamentally is, in terms of body movement: a crossover is a quick lateral redirection of the body's direction of travel, executed by planting and pushing off one foot to move diagonally the other way while the torso continues facing forward rather than turning. A spin move is a full turn of the body, pivoting on one foot, that reverses the direction the torso faces while the player continues moving forward along a new path. A stepback is a backward shift of the body away from the direction it had just been moving, pushing off to create distance before settling into a stationary stance. A between-the-legs move is one hand reaching briefly downward and across the body into the space between the knees, after which the body continues moving in a new direction. A dribble, in the general sense, is ordinary sustained forward or lateral movement of the body, without a sharp redirection, a full rotation, a backward shift, or a downward reach across the body. Base your identification on the whole sequence of movement described below, not only its starting and ending position.

Based on this movement data (and the known outcome above), analyse the attacker's play, Player 1. Your response must contain exactly:
1. Your best identification of the specific tactical move Player 1 used in this moment (a short phrase describing the footwork/ball-handling technique), based only on the movement data.
2. One positive observation - something Player 1 did well during this moment.
3. Exactly three alternative tactical moves Player 1 could have made instead, written in simple, beginner-friendly language a new player could understand.

Always refer to the players as "Player 1" and "Player 2" - never use any other name or label for them. Do not include any section, heading, or commentary other than the three items above.

Respond with ONLY this JSON object, no other text:
{
  "identified_move": "<short phrase>",
  "positive_observation": "<one sentence>",
  "alternative_moves": ["<move 1>", "<move 2>", "<move 3>"]
}
